name: The Ranch at Rock Creek
address: 79 Carriage House Lane, Philipsburg, MT 59858, United States
tagline: An all-inclusive cattle ranch of 6,600 acres in the Montana mountains.
description:
The Ranch at Rock Creek is a guest ranch 20 miles outside Philipsburg, in Granite County, Montana, at 5,200 feet. It covers 6,600 acres, which the ranch equates to 10 square miles, with four miles of Rock Creek, a Blue Ribbon fishery that flows into the Clark Fork. The land sits at the base of the John Long Mountains, with the Sapphire range to the north and the Pintler peaks to the south, near Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest and the Anaconda-Pintler Wilderness. The ranch prints its position as latitude 46.256434 and longitude 113.52213 west. Packages can be sent to 79 Carriage House Lane, Philipsburg, MT 59858.

The homestead follows the Homestead Act of 1862 and was taken up by W. W. Shaffer and P. W. White. A nineteenth-century barn remains, and the land has stayed a working cattle ranch. In 2007, after a 20-year search, owner Jim Manley turned the homestead into the guest ranch. Capacity is 125 guests across 31 accommodation units: nine suites in the Granite Lodge, ten canvas cabins, nine luxury homes and three Historic Barn accommodations. The accommodations page also refers to five ranch peaks.

The rate is all-inclusive: meals, unlimited premium beer, wine and spirits, activities, gear and airport transfers. A 25 percent Ranch Fee is added and covers lodging tax, gratuities, phone calls, Wi-Fi and in-room snacks. Spa treatments, the Mercantile, reserve-list wine, float trips and fishing licences are charged apart. Dining runs from 7:30 am to 10:00 pm in shared rooms. There is no in-room dining. Venues include the Granite Lodge dining room, the Flagstone, a pastoral picnic, the Buckle Barn and the Blue Canteen. The Buckle Barn covers 5,500 square feet and has a wood-fired grill faced with repurposed John Deere tractor parts. A children's menu is served. The Silver Dollar Saloon has billiards, poker, shuffleboard, karaoke, table tennis, a private movie theater, four bowling lanes and outdoor s'mores.

The Rod and Gun Club arranges 45 activities through the year, from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, with two a day suggested. They include horseback riding, fly fishing, hiking, mountain biking, archery, a ropes course and zip line, sapphire mining, and, in winter, cross-country skiing and snowmobiling. Flint's Forest Rangers is for children aged 4 to 12. The fitness centre in the Carriage House is open from 6:00 am to 10:00 pm, and there is a pool and a hot tub.

Missoula International Airport, MSO, is a 1.5-hour drive, and the transfer is included, as are transfers from Helena, Bozeman, Butte and Anaconda. Up to two pets may stay in a Luxury Home, the Historic Barn, the Trapper Cabin or the Sweetgrass Cabin for 100 dollars a night. Dogs stay on a leash, and pets are not taken in Granite Lodge rooms or in the dining rooms. Forbes Travel Guide lists the ranch at Five Stars, which the ranch presents as the first such rating for a ranch. It is also a member of Leading Hotels of the World and of Relais and Chateaux.
